facts.text: McGregor was originally called McGregor Springs, named after Dr. Gregor Carmichael McGregor who granted the railroad right‑of‑way.
The town’s early economy boomed with hotels, a national bank, a washing‑machine factory, a tannery, a cottonseed oil mill, and artesian waterworks.
McGregor Industrial Park sits on the site of a former Naval Weapons Reserve Plant, linking the town to military history.
Route 84 runs through McGregor’s center, connecting it 17 miles northeast to Waco and 20 miles west to Gatesville.
McGregor straddles McLennan and Coryell counties, placing part of the city in the Waco metro area and the other in the Killeen‑Temple‑Fort Hood metro area.
